en: This way, Aniki.
Ino's waitin' over at the dock.
Aniki. We need t'hurry.
Let's get movin', Aniki.
We're jus' about t'the boat, Aniki!
Hey, this way!
Everythin's ready fer ya!
Jus' get on over here!
Gotcha! Thanks, I really owe ya!

Fisherman friend o' mine said
he saw a suspicious-lookin' ship!

No doubt, the ones drivin' that
ship're the ones what took yer baby.
Where're they headin'?

Well y'know how they keep the cargo floatin'
on a separate island by the shipyard?
'Parently they're tryin' t'hide there!

A separate island for cargo?
What do you mean?

It'll make sense soon. Come t'think of it,
that'd be a great place t'store a boat.
By the way, where's Masuzoe?

He ran off when they started
attackin' us at the shrine.

Y'oughta jus' forget about him. We don't
gotta protect that monster, boss.
Don't be mean, Tagashira.

I'm wonderin' who took Haruto t'begin
with, though. D'ya know, Aniki?
It was the Jingweon Mafia.

I'm certain of that.
Joon-gi Han was there, too.
They're in Hiroshima?

Even so, I'm sure Tsuneo Iwami
is the one givin' the orders.

Patriarch. There's something
I still can't quite wrap my head around.

The connection between Onomichi
and the Saio Triad.

You said Yuta's been living in Onomichi
ever since he was a small child.

It seems like the <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind> Masuzoe and
Tatsukawa had taken root here, too.

There must be more to this
than you're choosing to let on.
You're pretty sharp.

Actually, the bond between the two
runs deeper than you'd expect.

Chairman Kurusu has been working with
the Saio Triad since before World War II.

Before the war?
That's more'n 70 years ago!

No shock there 'bout the chairman,
but I doubt Lo's that old.

You're right. Lo's father was the one
in charge of the Saio back then.

They stopped talkin' after the war,
but negotiations picked back up 30 years ago.

That's roughly about when
the Saio passed down to Lo.
30 years ago?

And the thing that brought them back
together? The <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind> business.

<font_kind=yakuza_italic>Heihaizi</font_kind> are basically Chinese children
who don't have any official documents.

So, Lo was working to smuggle
those children into Onomichi.

It was all thanks to Chairman Kurusu
that he managed to pull it off.

The chairman even helped forge
documents for the smuggled <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind>.

With his help, almost 10,000 children
had new lives under the rising sun.

Back in my heyday, I actually
helped out a bit with that.
You did? Y'never told us anythin'.

I still got all sorts of secrets
I haven't clued you guys in on.

Patriarch. What about
Chairman Kurusu's son, Tsuneo?
Was he involved with the <font_kind=yakuza_italic>heihaizi</font_kind>, too?

Hm? Yeah, I'm sure Tsuneo has
his own deal going with Lo.

I see. So that's the bond that ties
Onomichi and the Saio Triad together.

Hold on a sec. Ain't there somethin'
else tyin' the two together, Aniki?

Remember? In Little Asia, Lo was talkin' about
how Onomichi had some kinda secret.
A secret? Coulda fooled me.
Well, uh... I think I may have an idea.
Do ya now?

I heard Chairman Kurusu's real influential
with all sortsa politician types.

Not jus' local ones, either.
I'm talkin' big-time government.

They say he's even got ties t'that Fixer guy
who controls all o' Japan behind the scenes.

Maybe he has all those connections 'cause
o' some hidden power nobody knows about.
Y'think that could be the secret of Onomichi?
Wait, what the hell's all this 'bout a fixer?
You mean Minoru Daidoji?
Daidoji?

Yeah, pretty sure that's his name.
Surprised y'know it.
I heard it on TV or somethin'.

Well, every single scandal after the war
wound up gettin' pinned on him somehow.
He's basically an old fart nobody likes.
But he's a government shadow, guys.

They say the oil crisis n' the bubble collapse
were both conspiracies by the Fixer.

Sounds like horse shit t'me. Y'been readin'
those damn tabloids again, huh?

Hey, it's jus' over there!
I can see it!

Aniki. That cargo's what they use
fer buildin' the ships.

It's more convenient fer 'em t'keep the stuff
out at sea instead o' in some dusty warehouse.
So, that's where Haruto is.

Sorry, Kiryu-san. Ino n' I are gonna
stay and watch over the boat.
Yeah, no problem.

Oh, and I wanna apologize fer
not telling you about your girl.
I just wasn't sure how to approach it.

But at the very least, I wanted to keep
the kid safe while I figured it out.
Look how things ended up, though.
Bring that baby back, Kiryu-san.

By the way, yer girl told me
something interesting.

Apparently she wanted to go back to Okinawa
once she was confident she could raise the kid.
Haruka said that?
That's why she hadn't told you 'bout the kid.

She wanted to be able to see you again
with her head held high. Y'know?

I promise... I'm going to do what it takes
to bring Haruto back safe, Patriarch.
(The number's blocked. Who could it be?)

You have my thanks for our fight earlier.
I assure you the child is safe, Kiryu-san.
You... Joon-gi Han!

However, I must ask you to depart this island.
Your presence here is quite unwelcome.

On top of that, I have one more
rather peculiar request to make of you.

If you comply, Haruto-kun will be returned
to you without so much as a scratch.
What do you want from us?

Allow me to clarify: This is a task for Yuta-kun.
Please convey my message to him.
I would like him to kill Big Lo of the Saio Triad.

Yuta-kun should be able to approach
his father in a way nobody else can.

Case in point, we've been unable to even
<font_kind=yakuza_italic>locate</font_kind> Lo, let alone get close to him.

The paradigm shifted upon your
invasion into Little Asia, though.

After all, that was the first time
Lo had shown himself in over two months.
I think I understand now.

You only took Haruto so
you could force Yuta to kill Lo!

You have three days. If Yuta-kun succeeds,
I doubt the Saio will let him live.
However, if he is unable to complete my task...
You'll kill Haruto?

I can't believe that. You would really
murder a child who can't even walk yet?

And all that talk of sportsmanship
you were so proud of before?

Didn't you say you value elegance
above everything else!?

You should have come to me before
pulling a stunt like this, Joon-gi Han.

Listen close. I'm coming to you, alone. No matter
how many of your men I have to go through.
If it's a fight you want, it's a fight you'll get!
Do you hear me!?

If you will indeed be coming by yourself,
I wouldn't turn you away, Kiryu-san.
Assuming you can make it to me, that is.
I anticipate your arrival.

What's going on, Kiryu-aniki?
What did Joon-gi Han want from you?

You already know the answer to that.
From this point forward, I'll be going alone.

Y'can't do that, Aniki! We got no idea
how many of 'em are waitin' fer ya.
Even yer gonna have trouble, Aniki.

If we all went together, who knows
what Han would do to Haruto.

This was the best deal I could make
in the time I had. Sorry.

As for Haruto, I promise I'll bring him back.
Just you wait.

You truly are a man of your word,
coming here all by yourself, Kiryu-san.

I told you I would fight through
whatever you could throw at me.

Alas, it would seem as though
I am the only one left standing.

No matter how you slice it,
this is the end of the Jingweon Mafia.
I have a question for you, though.

The one who's been supporting your
resurgence... It's Tsuneo Iwami, isn't it?

Indeed. After the Little Asia fire,
Iwami approached us with a proposal.

Our part was simply to fan the flames of
war between the Tojo Clan and the Saio.

I see. And he'd give you enough money to
buy up half of Kamurocho, Stardust included.

It was a rather generous offer. Only after
we had completed our task, of course.

We were unfortunately unable to kill Big Lo,
but we did manage to take out his son, Jimmy.

That's right. We were working
with your friend Tatsukawa-kun as well.

In fact, I was even present in Kamurocho
when he struck Haruka Sawamura in his car.

We were tasked with watching over Tatsukawa-kun
to make sure he actually kidnapped the baby.

Similar to our present situation, we hoped
we could force Yuta-kun to assassinate Lo.
Fine, but why did Tatsukawa hit Haruka!?

Simply put, that was a mistake.
It was an outcome nobody wanted.

A few days before the accident, Tatsukawa-kun
found Haruka in the town where Hirose hid her.

It must have been an extraordinary
surprise for her to see him there.

But, he made quite a compelling
argument to gain Haruka's trust.

He claimed he would help her, even
if it meant disobeying orders.

Apparently that's the reason he gave for
wanting to move her somewhere "safer."

She must have thought it strange that he would
pass up such a clear opportunity to attack her.

Beyond that, all he told her before he left
was to bring the child with her to Kamurocho.

It makes sense that she would be suspicious
of his reason for wanting her there.

Tatsukawa... Why did he have
to lure Haruka out to Kamurocho?

The village she was hiding in was minuscule.
Even a minor disturbance would be big news.

If we wanted Yuta-kun to succeed
in his assassination of Lo...

...We had to ensure there was no chance
the Saio could find out we kidnapped the baby.

To that end, Kamurocho was
the perfect place to carry out our plan.

Nobody in that pit would bat an eye
at a girl screaming about her kidnapped son.
But on that day...

After they met up in an underground parking lot,
Tatsukawa-kun demanded Haruka get in his car.

Had she agreed, she and Haruto would have
been handed over to Iwami as planned.

However, Haruka's well-placed mistrust of
Tatsukawa kept her from getting in the car.

Had her grip loosened even a little,
who knows what could have happened.

Perhaps the child would have been
smeared across the pavement.

However, she refused to let go
of her son, at the cost of herself.
The strength of a mother is truly incredible.

I get it.
You bastards hurt Haruka.
An unfortunate side effect.

Regardless, we were simply following
the orders given to us by Tsuneo Iwami.

Han. Are you telling me all of this now
so my mind can be at peace when I kill you?

Not at all. I told you because I'll no longer
have the chance once I reduce you to a corpse.
And to die not knowing would be a shame.

Now then, we can finally settle
this quarrel once and for all.
Nobody can get in our way anymore.
This time, we fight to the death, Kiryu-san!

This will be the Jingweon Mafia's
final flourish!
Kiryu-aniki! Yer okay!
I brought Haruto back for you, Yuta.
Ha-Haruto?

I'm sorry...
I'm so sorry, Haruto!

You must've been really scared.
Because of me, you and yer mom...
Hey. Let's head home, you guys.
Joon-gi Han... got shot!?

Yeah. I'm not sure who hit him,
or even where they shot from.

By the time I looked back,
the shooter was gone.
I'd guess it was one of Tsuneo's boys.

Joon-gi Han must've paid the price
fer messing things up so bad.
But before he got shot...

He said Chairman Kurusu is the one
protecting the secret of Onomichi.
Big Lo was worried about that secret, too.

I'm starting to think it's more
important than we realize.

It might have something to do with why Iwami
and the Saio are at each other's throats, too.

Hold on a sec. So yer tellin' me the chairman's
responsible fer all this shit that's goin' down?

No. It's not fair to blame Chairman Kurusu
for his son's actions.

Truth is, Tsuneo's less obedient
to his father than he lets on.

The chairman was never planning for Tsuneo
to inherit control of his dealings.

In fact, the whole reason he promoted Koshimizu
to Yomei Captain was to groom him as his successor.
But it backfired.

At some point or another, Tsuneo
sweet-talked Koshimizu onto his side.

Tsuneo's turned out to be more ambitious
than any of us woulda thought, for sure.
Chairman Kurusu's real frustrated.

Patriarch. How exactly
do you know Chairman Kurusu?
Well, we're old drinkin' buds, basically.
What? Y'serious!?

It's nice talking to someone
my own age fer a change.

He's never mentioned a thing to me about
Onomichi having some big secret, though.
No idea what all that's about.

For all we know, it's some old
rumor that just got out of hand.

Um, I've been wonderin', Aniki...
What're y'gonna do with Haruto tonight?

If y'leave him here, it'd be a cinch fer
the main family t'find him again.
